# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

## 1. LOOP-DRAWING GAMES
*The primary goal is to draw a single continuous closed loop*

### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
Games where the loop may pass freely through cells, subject only to clue constraints

- **Masyu** — Loop must navigate black circles (turn + straight) and white circles (straight + turn adjacent)
- **Slitherlink** — Loop drawn between dots; numbers indicate how many sides of a cell are used
- **Yajilin** — Loop avoids numbered/black cells; arrow-numbers indicate black cell counts in a direction

### 1.2 Directional / Wind-Constrained Loop
- **Nagareru** — Loop direction is fixed by arrows; wind cells restrict movement direction

### 1.3 Gate/Sequence-Constrained Loop
- **Suraromu** — Loop must pass through all "Gates" exactly once in a numbered sequence

### 1.4 Circle/Midpoint-Constrained Loop
- **Mid-loop** — Black circles must be the midpoint of a straight segment of the loop

### 1.5 Room-Constrained Loop
Games where the loop interacts with defined regions

- **Dotchi-Loop** — Loop passes through white circles; within each bold-line area, all circles are either all straight or all turning
- **Moon-or-Sun** — Loop passes through each room once; alternates between visiting all moons or all suns per room

---

## 2. PATH / CONNECTION GAMES
*The goal is to draw paths or connections between specific points, without forming a closed loop*

### 2.1 Island Connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — Connect numbered islands with bridges (max 2 per pair); all islands must be connected

### 2.2 Pair Connection
- **Numberlink** — Connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-branching lines that fill the grid

### 2.3 Movement / Migration
- **Satogaeri** — Move circles a specified number of cells so each bold-line region contains exactly one circle
- **Yosenabe** — Move numbered circles into gray areas so totals match; arrows show straight-line movement

---

## 3. REGION DIVISION GAMES
*The goal is to partition the grid into defined regions or blocks*

### 3.1 Rectangle/Square Division
- **Shikaku** — Divide grid into rectangles, each containing exactly one number equal to its cell count
- **Choco Banana** — Divide into regions; black regions must be rectangles/squares, white regions must not be

### 3.2 Fixed-Size Polyomino Division
- **Five Cells** — Divide grid into pentominoes (exactly 5 cells each); numbers indicate boundary line count
- **LITS** — Color one tetromino per bold-line region; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch; colored cells must connect

### 3.3 Variable-Size Block Division
- **Fillomino** — Fill grid with numbered blocks where each block's size equals its number; same-size blocks cannot touch
- **Sashigane** — Divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark the bend, arrows point toward the bend

### 3.4 Paired/Symmetric Division
- **Double Choco** — Divide into blocks each containing a white and gray area of identical shape and size
- **Nuritwin** — Each bold-line region contains exactly two same-sized shaded blocks that don't touch each other

### 3.5 Evolving/Sequential Block Division
- **Evolomino** — Blocks along an arrow route grow by one cell each step without rotation or flipping

---

## 4. CELL-SHADING / PAINTING GAMES
*The goal is to determine which cells to color black (or shade)*

### 4.1 Connectivity-Constrained Shading
Games where shaded and/or unshaded cells must satisfy global connectivity rules

- **Nurikabe** — Black cells form a connected wall; white cell groups each contain exactly one number indicating their size; no 2×2 black squares
- **Heyawake** — Shade cells per room counts; no two shaded cells touch; white cells cannot span more than two rooms in a line
- **Hitori** — Shade cells so no number repeats in any row/column; shaded cells don't touch; white cells stay connected
- **Kurodoko** — Shade cells so numbered white cells "see" exactly as many white cells as their value; black cells don't touch

### 4.2 Shape-Constrained Shading
- **Choco Banana** *(also listed under 3.1)* — Black groups must be rectangular; white groups must not be rectangular
- **Shakashaka** — Place triangles in cells so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares; numbers count adjacent triangles

### 4.3 Sum/Count-Constrained Shading
- **Kurotto** — Circles show the total count of connected black cells extending from them in all four directions
- **Usowan** — Shade cells; each bold-line rectangle contains exactly one "wrong" number (one number misreports its adjacent shaded count)
- **Norinori** — Each bold-line region contains exactly two shaded cells; shaded cells pair up as dominoes

### 4.4 Gravity/Drop-Constrained Shading
- **Sto-stone** — Shade cells per room counts; when all shaded cells "drop" downward, they fill exactly the bottom half of the grid

### 4.5 Maze-Creating Shading
- **Nurimeizu** — Shade whole rooms to create walls; a unique shortest path from S to G passes through all circles and no triangles; no 2×2 uniformity

### 4.6 Tile-Based Shading
- **Tilepaint** — Entire bold-line tiles are shaded or not; diagonal-number cells constrain counts in their row/column segment; solution depicts an object outline

### 4.7 Promontory Shading
- **Nurimisaki** — Circled cells are "promontories" (white, with exactly one white neighbor); numbers indicate straight-line white cell length from the promontory; white cells connect; no 2×2 uniformity

---

## 5. NUMBER-PLACEMENT GAMES
*The goal is to place or fill numbers into cells according to logical constraints*

### 5.1 Latin Square / Uniqueness Constraint
- **Sudoku** — Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box with no repeats

### 5.2 Room-Based Number Filling
- **Ripple Effect** — Each bold-line room contains 1 through N (room size); duplicate numbers in a row/column must be separated by at least that number of cells
- **Makaro** — Each room contains 1 through N; arrow-black-cells indicate which neighbor holds the largest value; same numbers in different rooms cannot be adjacent

### 5.3 Block-Size Encoding
- **Fillomino** *(also listed under 3.3)* — Numbers encode the size of the block they belong to
- **Chained Block** — Black cell groups ("blocks") are labeled with their size or "?"; blocks must chain corner-to-corner; no two same-shaped blocks in one chain

### 5.4 Crossword-Style Number Placement
- **Nansuke** — Fill white cells with digits from a given list of numbers placed horizontally or vertically

### 5.5 Snake Placement
- **Hebi** — Place snake segments numbered 1 (head) to 5 (tail) in white cells; snakes cannot touch each other; directional visibility rules restrict placement; black cells give clues about nearest snake segment

---

## 6. SYMBOL / MARK PLACEMENT GAMES
*The goal is to place non-numeric symbols or marks into cells*

### 6.1 Light Placement
- **Akari** — Place light bulbs in white cells; numbered black cells indicate adjacent bulb count; every white cell must be illuminated; bulbs cannot illuminate each other

### 6.2 Line/Stroke Placement
- **Juosan** — Fill every cell with "—" or "|"; bold-line territories constrain the difference in counts; "—" cannot extend more than 2 cells vertically; "|" cannot extend more than 2 cells horizontally

### 6.3 Triangle Placement
- **Shakashaka** *(also listed under 4.2)* — Place half-cell triangles so white remainders are always rectangular

### 6.4 Square/Block Placement with Growth Rule
- **Evolomino** *(also listed under 3.5)* — Place squares along arrow routes; each successive block adds one cell

---

## 7. OBJECT-DRAWING / PENCIL-LINE GAMES
*The goal is to draw lines representing physical objects (pencils, paths) with specific structural rules*

- **Pencils** — Identify pencil bodies (straight strips) and draw lines from their tips; line length matches the number in the pencil; lines cannot cross or branch

---

## Cross-Cutting Structural Dimensions

| Dimension | Categories Present |
|---|---|
| **Primary output** | Shading, Number fill, Loop, Path, Region division, Symbol placement |
| **Constraint scope** | Local (adjacent cells), Regional (bold-line rooms), Global (connectivity, uniqueness) |
| **Clue type** | Count clues, Directional clues, Shape clues, Sequence clues, Sum clues |
| **Connectivity requirement** | Loop (closed path), Tree/network (Hashiwokakero), Connected region (Nurikabe white/black), None |
| **Region structure** | Pre-defined bold-line rooms, Player-defined divisions, Implicit (row/column) |
| **Uniqueness constraint** | Present (Sudoku, Hitori, Fillomino), Absent |
